scope: Backend, API, and integration contract review only. No product scope, first platform, persistence technology, or implementation stack is approved, so this record makes no implementation-readiness, release, or production claim.

dependencyEvidence.sharedBusinessRuleBoundary: One UI-independent download domain service owns state transitions and policies. Desktop UI, filesystem, browser, persistence, and other adapters consume that service and may not redefine pause, resume, retry, cancellation, destination-conflict, completion, or recovery rules.

commands.name: add
commands.outcome: Create a durable queued download only after URL and destination inputs pass approved validation.

commands.name: pause
commands.outcome: Stop transfer safely and enter paused without presenting partial content as complete.

commands.name: resume
commands.outcome: Resume only after validating server range behavior and remote identity; otherwise return an explicit restart-required result.

commands.name: cancel
commands.outcome: Enter cancelled using the human-approved retain-or-delete partial-file policy.

commands.name: retry
commands.outcome: Return to queued while retaining the preceding failure information for adapters.

commands.name: complete
commands.outcome: Enter completed only after integrity checks and atomic finalization succeed.

invariants: Adapters request commands through the shared domain service and receive typed results; adapters do not mutate state directly.
Every accepted command and resulting state is persisted atomically before success is exposed.
Partial files and incomplete metadata are never represented as completed.
Retry and resume are distinct: retry re-queues work, while resume requires validated byte-range and remote-identity evidence.
Destination conflict resolution occurs before finalization and uses only a human-approved overwrite, rename, or cancel policy.
Unknown or stale command versions fail closed without changing durable state.

serviceBoundary.transport: In-process application service by default; no network API is justified for the baseline desktop product.
serviceBoundary.concurrency: Commands carry the last observed state version. A stale version returns a conflict result rather than overwriting a newer transition.
serviceBoundary.privacy: Results and logs exclude credentials, authorization headers, signed URL query values, and unrestricted local paths unless explicitly required by the trusted local UI.

adapterContracts.responsibility: HTTP transfer, redirects, bounded retry, range negotiation, integrity evidence, and resource limits
atomic metadata reads/writes, optimistic version checks, restart recovery, and migrations
destination access, partial-file lifecycle, atomic finalization, conflict execution, and file reveal
present domain state, submit commands, and expose accessible outcomes
if later approved, authenticate and validate versioned local messages with explicit consent

recoveryContract.startup: Load durable records, reconcile active work with process reality, and transition unfinished active transfers to interrupted before accepting commands.
recoveryContract.partialFiles: Associate each partial file with one download identifier and remote identity; quarantine or report unmatched artifacts rather than finalizing them.
recoveryContract.resumeValidation: Require a valid range response and matching approved remote identity metadata before appending bytes.
recoveryContract.finalization: Flush and close the partial file, perform the approved integrity check, resolve destination policy, atomically move where the platform supports it, and persist completed last.
recoveryContract.failureBehavior: Disk exhaustion, permission loss, invalid ranges, identity changes, and failed finalization return explicit typed failures without silent completion or destructive cleanup.

securityIntegrationRequirements: Allow only approved URL schemes and validate every redirect destination.
Keep authentication material in an approved credential facility; never persist it in download metadata or logs.
Apply bounded connection, retry, concurrency, memory, disk, and response-metadata limits.
Treat filenames and server metadata as untrusted; normalize through the platform filesystem adapter and prevent path traversal.
Do not execute, preview, or automatically open downloaded content from the backend service.
Browser integration and update endpoints remain deferred until their trust boundaries and ownership are approved.

verificationScenarios.scenario: State-table tests reject every undefined transition and stale state version without persistence changes.
A controlled range server proves valid resume appends correctly and invalid or changed identity produces restart_required without corruption.
Process termination during metadata write, partial-file write, and finalization restores an interrupted or completed state consistently after restart.
Disk exhaustion, permission denial, and destination conflicts preserve the prior valid artifact and return typed recovery actions.
Redirect, path traversal, oversized metadata, credential, and sensitive-log fixtures are rejected or redacted.
Representative concurrent transfers stay within approved CPU, memory, disk, connection, and bandwidth budgets.

traceability.limitation: Platform-specific implementation awaits approved platform and supported versions.
Browser capture, authentication, segmented transfers, scheduling, bandwidth controls, telemetry, and automatic updates remain unapproved or deferred.
Independent disposition is reserved for ENG-15.

Approved performance budgets and integrity method
exitEvidence: Shared domain service implementation consumed by all adapters
Controlled HTTP and filesystem integration tests

implementationNotes: No application implementation, database migration, infrastructure mutation, deployment, credential use, or Git-history operation was performed by WS-04.
The contract intentionally avoids selecting a language, framework, database, network API, or platform before accountable decisions exist.
User-visible behavior must be verified through the real desktop runtime or equivalent integration surface after an implementation exists.
knownRisks: Resume behavior can silently corrupt files unless byte ranges and remote identity are validated together.
Persistence and filesystem finalization cannot be specified fully until supported platforms and storage technology are selected.
Cancellation cleanup, destination overwrite, integrity method, authentication, and retry limits are product or architecture decisions still unresolved.
A network-facing API would add authentication and local attack-surface obligations and is not justified by current approved evidence.
No executable application exists, so runtime, integration, performance, security, or recovery outcomes have not been demonstrated.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
